page.layout: One column of running text, set in the middle of the page. Page number "152" at top left, running head "NOTÆ." at top right. No marginal notes. Catchword "ejus" at the foot, right.

main_text.l: notus Arabismus iste. من دخل ظفار حمير
Qui Dhafarum ingreditur, (urbs ea, Regum Hamyarensium
sedes) Hamyarismum addiscat, quae verbum in pro-
verbium abierunt, quo monetur quis eorum quibus
cohabitat, moribus|se accommodare. Hinc autem (uti
diximus) patet Hamyarensium Dialectum ad Hebrai-
cam vel Syriacam, sive Chaldaicam in quibusdam,
propius accedere, (ut & ipsos ad Judaismum incli-
nasse in superioribus vidimus) ذن[?] enim Hamyarin-
fibus[?] idem sonat ac Hebraeis ישב[?] Syris & Chaldaeis
יתב[?] a quo in Imperativo ישב[?] Sedere. at communi Ara-
bum dialecto contrariam habet notionem, Saltandi sc.
vel Subsiliendi. Praeterea in Regis responso quod
عربيت[?] litera claudatur quod Arabes per ꝫ[?] efferre
solent, Syrismum etiam sapere videtur. Per linguam
autem istam cujus peritiae operam dedisse Arabes as-
serit Author noster, Dialectum istam Koraifhitarum
defaecatam & politam praecipuè intelligi credo, quae
quâ ratione caeteris elegantior evaserit describit Jal-
aloddinus in lib. Mezh. c. 9. scil. quòd dum Templi
Meccani aedituï essent & Arabia centrum incolerent
non solùm à caeteris Gentibus (quarum vicinia &
commercio aliarum Tribuum sermo vitii aliquid
contraxerat) remotiores essent, sed & confluentibus
undequaque Meccam Arabibus tum religionis ergò,
tum ut lites suas ad ipsos componendas deferrent, ex
eorum sermone & carminibus puriores ac elegantio-
res quascunque sive dictiones, sive loquendi formu-
las & phrases, selectas, suas facerent, adeò ut in ipsorum
Dialectum omnes universi quaquâ patet Arabismi
elegantiae confluxerint. Linguae autem suae in Enco-
mium multa congerunt, atque inter caetera, immensa
ejus[catchword]

page.notes: Arabic and Hebrew words are copied from the scan and are doubtful where marked [?]: the Arabic after "enim", the Hebrew forms ישב and יתב, and the Arabic word before "litera". The Hebrew and Arabic at the start of the first line is read with reasonable confidence. The character after "per" is unclear. "Hamyarin-fibus" at the line end is doubtful. The word "ejus" appears at the foot as a catchword and is also the last word of the text, so it is printed once in the paragraph and once in the catchword. Long s is written as s throughout.
